stem: If \(\vec{v_1} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + \hat{k}\) and \(\vec{v_2} = \hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}\), determine the magnitude of \(\vec{v_1} + \vec{v_2}\).
our_solution:
Add the two vectors component by component, then take the magnitude of the sum.
\(\vec{v_1} + \vec{v_2} = (3 + 1)\hat{i} + (4 - 1)\hat{j} + (1 - 1)\hat{k} = 4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}\)
\(|\vec{v_1} + \vec{v_2}| = \sqrt{4^{2} + 3^{2} + 0^{2}} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = \sqrt{25}\)
\(|\vec{v_1} + \vec{v_2}| = 5\)

stem: For \(\vec{v_1} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}\) and \(\vec{v_2} = -6\hat{i} + 5\hat{j}\), determine the magnitude and direction of \(\vec{v_1} + \vec{v_2}\).
our_solution:
Add component by component, then use \(|\vec{R}| = \sqrt{R_x^{2} + R_y^{2}}\) and \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{R_y}{R_x}\).
\(\vec{v_1} + \vec{v_2} = (2 - 6)\hat{i} + (-3 + 5)\hat{j} = -4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}\)
\(|\vec{v_1} + \vec{v_2}| = \sqrt{(-4)^{2} + 2^{2}} = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}\)
\(\tan\theta = \dfrac{R_y}{R_x} = \dfrac{2}{-4} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\)
\(\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\) with the \(x\)-axis.
Because \(R_x\) is negative and \(R_y\) positive, the resultant lies in the second quadrant, so measured anticlockwise from the \(+x\)-axis the direction is \(180^{\circ} - 26^{\circ}34' = 153^{\circ}26'\).
Magnitude \(2\sqrt{5}\), direction \(\tan^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\) with the \(x\)-axis.

stem: Find a vector which is parallel to \(\vec{v} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j}\) and has a magnitude 10.
our_solution:
A vector parallel to \(\vec{v}\) with a required magnitude is that magnitude times the unit vector along \(\vec{v}\).
\(|\vec{v}| = \sqrt{1^{2} + (-2)^{2}} = \sqrt{5}\)
\(\hat{v} = \dfrac{\vec{v}}{|\vec{v}|} = \dfrac{\hat{i} - 2\hat{j}}{\sqrt{5}}\)
Required vector \(= 10\,\hat{v} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{5}}\hat{i} - \dfrac{20}{\sqrt{5}}\hat{j}\)
On rationalising this is \(2\sqrt{5}\,\hat{i} - 4\sqrt{5}\,\hat{j}\), whose magnitude is \(\sqrt{20 + 80} = 10\) as required.
The vector is \(\dfrac{10}{\sqrt{5}}\hat{i} - \dfrac{20}{\sqrt{5}}\hat{j}\).

Write the vector product as a determinant, taking the \(\hat{k}\) component of each vector as zero.
\(\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & 5 & 0 \end{vmatrix}\)
\(= \hat{i}\,(3 \times 0 - 0 \times 5) - \hat{j}\,(2 \times 0 - 0 \times 3) + \hat{k}\,(2 \times 5 - 3 \times 3)\)
\(= 0\,\hat{i} - 0\,\hat{j} + (10 - 9)\hat{k}\)
\(\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \hat{k}\)

stem: Determine the vector product of \(\vec{v_1} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}\) and \(\vec{v_2} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\),
our_solution:
Write the vector product as a determinant and expand it.
\(\vec{v_1} \times \vec{v_2} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \end{vmatrix}\)
\(= \hat{i}\,\big((3)(-3) - (-1)(2)\big) - \hat{j}\,\big((2)(-3) - (-1)(1)\big) + \hat{k}\,\big((2)(2) - (3)(1)\big)\)
\(= \hat{i}\,(-9 + 2) - \hat{j}\,(-6 + 1) + \hat{k}\,(4 - 3)\)
\(\vec{v_1} \times \vec{v_2} = -7\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + \hat{k}\)

stem: Given \(\vec{v_1} = 5\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}\) and \(\vec{v_2} = a\hat{i} - 6\hat{j}\) are perpendicular to each other, determine the value of \(a\).
our_solution:
Perpendicular vectors have zero scalar product, so set \(\vec{v_1} \cdot \vec{v_2} = 0\).
\(\vec{v_1} \cdot \vec{v_2} = (5)(a) + (2)(-6) = 5a - 12\)
\(5a - 12 = 0\)
\(a = \dfrac{12}{5}\)

stem:
Obtain derivatives of the following functions:
(i) \(x \sin x\)
(ii) \(x^{4} + \cos x\)
(iii) \(x/\sin x\)
book_answer: (i) \(\sin x + x \cos x\), (ii) \(4x^{3} - \sin x\), (iii) \(\dfrac{1}{\sin x} - \dfrac{x \cos x}{\sin^{2} x}\)
our_solution:
(i) By the product rule \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(f_1 f_2) = f_1\dfrac{df_2}{dx} + \dfrac{df_1}{dx}f_2\), with \(f_1 = x\) and \(f_2 = \sin x\):
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x \sin x) = x\cos x + (1)\sin x = \sin x + x\cos x\)

(ii) Differentiating term by term, using \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{n}) = nx^{n-1}\) and \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cos x) = -\sin x\):
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{4} + \cos x) = 4x^{3} - \sin x\)

(iii) By the quotient rule \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{f_1}{f_2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{f_2}\dfrac{df_1}{dx} - \dfrac{f_1}{f_2^{2}}\dfrac{df_2}{dx}\), with \(f_1 = x\) and \(f_2 = \sin x\):
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x}{\sin x}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sin x} - \dfrac{x\cos x}{\sin^{2} x}\)

The derivatives are \(\sin x + x\cos x\), \(4x^{3} - \sin x\) and \(\dfrac{1}{\sin x} - \dfrac{x\cos x}{\sin^{2} x}\).

stem:
Evaluate the following integral:
(i) \(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin x\,dx\)
(ii) \(\displaystyle\int_{1}^{5} x\,dx\)
our_solution:
(i) The antiderivative of \(\sin x\) is \(-\cos x\), so evaluate it between the limits.
\(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin x\,dx = \left[-\cos x\right]_{0}^{\pi/2} = -\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \left(-\cos 0\right) = 0 + 1 = 1\)

(ii) Using \(\displaystyle\int x^{n}dx = \dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\) with \(n = 1\):
\(\displaystyle\int_{1}^{5} x\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{5} = \dfrac{25}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{24}{2} = 12\)

The values of the integrals are 1 and 12.
